title: Panelyzer: offline spectral flow cytometry panel design
description:
Panelyzer is an offline, single-file tool for designing spectral flow cytometry panels. It runs entirely in the browser from one HTML file and makes no network requests.

For a chosen instrument (Cytek Aurora 5L, Sony ID7000 5- and 7-laser, or a custom layout) it computes fluor signatures, cosine similarity, the complexity index, noise amplification and an estimated spillover-spreading matrix from a photon-noise model of least-squares unmixing. Optimizers suggest low-complexity fluor sets, assign markers to fluors using expression, brightness and co-expression, and rank the fluors that best fit a new marker. Signatures come from 271 FPbase spectra, approximations for dyes FPbase lacks, and Honeychrome's measured reference libraries, with detector-gain calibration of simulated dyes. It imports Cytek-style panel CSVs, single-stain FCS files, reference CSVs and Honeychrome experiments. A companion Honeychrome plugin, Panel Check, measures spillover spreading from single-stain controls and exports a calibration Panelyzer imports.

Validation (simulated vs measured spectra, and the linear algebra against NumPy) is described in docs/VALIDATION.md in the repository.

AI use. Panelyzer was developed with substantial assistance from Claude (Anthropic), a generative AI model, which wrote most of the code, tests and documentation under the direction of Cole Batty. Cole Batty defined the requirements and design, tested it on real panels and Honeychrome experiments, and is responsible for the project. See the README for details.

Spectra: FPbase (CC BY-SA 4.0); Honeychrome reference libraries (LGPL-3.0). Code: LGPL-3.0-or-later.
